You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

def segments(cells):
    segs=[]; seen=set(); cells=set(cells)
    for p in sorted(cells):
        if p in seen:continue
        # vertical run up/down from p
        for d in [(1,0),(-1,0),(0,1),(0,-1)]:
            q=p+d
            while q in cells and not(0<=q[0]<H and 0<=q[1]<W):break
            if q in cells:
                s=set(p);path=[p,q]
                x,y=q
                while True:
                    x+=d[0];y+=d[1]
                    if not(0<=x<H and 0<=y<W) or x not in cells:break
                    path.append((x,y))
                segs.append(path); seen|=set(path); break
    return segs
H=len(g);W=len(g[0])
for seg in segments(pos): print(seg[:6],'...',seg[-3:])

import os,glob,re,json
from collections import Counter,deque
def load():
    d=os.path.normpath(os.environ['RLM_SESSION_DIR'])
    t=open(d+'/../../sessions/'+os.path.basename(d)+'.jsonl').read().replace('\\n','\n'); G={}
    for m in re.finditer(r'(Demo pair \d+ (?:input|output)|Test input) \((\d+)x(\d+)\):\n',t):
        k,h,w=m[1],int(m[2]),int(m[3])
        rows=[r.split() for r in t[m.end():].split('\n')[:h]]
        if k not in G and all(len(r)==w and all(x.isdigit() for x in r) for r in rows):
            G[k]=[[int(x) for x in r] for r in rows]
    return G

def f(gv):
    g=[row[:] for row in gv]; H,W=len(g),len(g[0])
    cnt=Counter(x for r in g for x in r); bg=cnt.most_common(1)[0][0]
    cs=comps(g,bg)

    res=g
    # arms: for each maximal straight run of B (>=2 cells), directions along it; walk from each end outward
    runs=[]
    seen=set(); 
    for dr,dc in ((1,0),(-1,0),(0,1),(0,-1)):
        pts=sorted(B)
        p=pts[0] if pts else None
        while p:
            d=[]
            q=p
            while True:
                nxt=(q[0]+dr,q[1]+dc)
                if nxt not in B: break
                d.append(nxt); q=nxt
            if len(d)>=1: runs.append((p,(dr,dc),d)); p=None

        p=None
    for _,dirs,d in runs:

                for c,n,cc in cs:
                    if nxt in set(cc): found=c; break
                if found: break
                q=nxt
            if found:
                for c in cc: res[c[0]][c[1]]=v
    return res

def load():
    d=os.path.normpath(os.environ['RLM_SESSION_DIR'])
    t=open(d+'/../../sessions/'+os.path.basename(d)+'.jsonl').read().replace('\\n','\n'); G={}
    for m in re.finditer(r'(Demo pair \d+ (?:input|output)|Test input) \((\d+)x(\d+)\):\n',t):
        k,h,w=m[1],int(m[2]),int(m[3])
        rows=[r.split() for r in t[m.end():].split('\n')[:h]]
        if k not in G and all(len(r)==w and all(x.isdigit() for x in r) for r in rows):
            G[k]=[[int(x) for x in r] for r in rows]
    return G
G=load()
for p in [4,5,6,7]:
    I=G[f'Demo pair {p} input']; O=G[f'Demo pair {p} output']
    bg=Counter(x for r in I for x in r).most_common(1)[0][0]
    ch=[(i,j,I[i][j],O[i][j]) for i in range(len(I)) for j in range(len(I[0])) if I[i][j]!=O[i][j]]
    print('=== demo',p,'bg',bg)
    for c,a,b in [(x,y,z) for x,y,z,_ in ch]: pass
    print('colors changed:', Counter((a,b) for _,_,a,b in ch))

    for s in tcobjs:

def nrm(cs): cs=set(cs); i0=min(a for a,b in cs); j0=min(b for a,b in cs); return tuple(sorted((a-i0,b-j0) for a,b in cs))
def dkeys(cells):
    ks=[]
    for tr in (lambda v:v, lambda v:[(i,-j) for i,j in v], lambda v:[(-i,j) for i,j in v], lambda v:[(-i,-j) for i,j in v], lambda v:[(j,i) for i,j in v], lambda v:[(-j,i) for i,j in v], lambda v:[(j,-i) for i,j in v]):
        ks.append(nrm(tr(list(cells))))
    return frozenset(ks)
def is_subshape(sub,tpl):
    # normalized subshape must fit inside template as consecutive region
    s,nm=nrm(sub),len(sub); t=len(tpl)
    if nm>t or len(s)>len(t): return False
    h=max(a for a,b in s)+1; w=max(b for a,b in s)+1
    th,hw=max(a for a,b in tpl)+1,max(b for a,b in tpl)+1
    if hw>th or w>hw: return False
    hs=[a for a,b in s]; hs2=[b for a,b in s]
    # try all offsets within bbox relative coords - brute force: place s into t
    ts=tuple(sorted((a,b) for a,b in tpl))
    Hh=len(ts); Ww=len(ts[0]) if ts else 0
    for da in range(th):
        for db in range(hw):
            ok=all((da+a,db+b) in set(ts) for a,b in s)
            if ok: return True
    return False

    res=[r[:] for r in I]; tc,mkcells=mk
    sk=dkeys(mkcells); chset=set()
    for c,s in C:
        if c!=tc and is_subshape(s,mkcells) and dkeys(s)&sk: pass
        # also test pure subshape without dihedral requirement first
